text:
alex: Declaring incident — SFO inference pool is degraded, GPU pod churn + queue backlog rising. I'm starting a controlled traffic shift to AMS. Tagging @emma @kai for triage and runbook updates.

sre_oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-17760. Priority: P1. Notifying oncall.

emma: I see elevated queue length on sfo-inference-01 (backlog ~620 requests). Some pods are in CrashLoopBackOff, likely driver/kernel OOMs.

kai: Confirmed. GPU memory pressure spikes correlated with a slow batch job that retried and filled the pool. Temp mitigation: scaling sfo nodegroup down and cordoning several problematic nodes to drain.

lee: I'm starting a gradual 10%/min traffic shift from sfo -> ams to avoid cold-start surge. Will monitor tail latency.

devops: Quick notes for the runbook: need a pre-check before manual shift: `kubectl get nodes -l region=sfo -o wide` and `kubectl top pods -n inference --containers`. Also add this one-liner to drain a node: 
```
kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
```

emma: Root cause hypothesis: a background retrain job (dataset-snapshotter) launched at midnight and pinned GPU memory, triggering eviction cascade. We didn't have a hard cap on batch job GPU requests.

kai: Action items (triage):
- kai: add a hard quota for background batch jobs in sfo (k8s LimitRange / resourcequota) — due EOD
- emma: add an alert rule for queue backlog crossing 400 for >5m (pager) — due today
- alex: update failover runbook to include cost-tagging and pre-warm step (see notes) — due tomorrow

alex: Runbook updates to include in this thread: 
1) Pre-failover checklist: confirm reserve pool >= 2x usual burst, ensure warm instances flagged `warm:true`.
2) Traffic-shift ramp policy: `shift_rate=10%/min`, pause if tail P95 > SLA for 3 consecutive minutes.
3) Cost tagging: add labels/annotations on ephemeral instances when triggered by failover: `failover_reason`, `failover_time`, `initiator` — helps chargeback and later cost analysis.

lee: Adding a short snippet for the ramp policy to the runbook: 
```
# pseudo
for step in 1..10:
  shift_fraction = step * 0.1
  update-weight(sfo, 1 - shift_fraction)
  update-weight(ams, shift_fraction)
  sleep 60
  if metric("p95_latency") > target: rollback and notify
```

devops: Note on cost: this incident created ~18h of on-demand GPU usage in AMS and a ~23% spike in monthly bill for affected workload. We should attach `cost_center` and `failover_reason` tags in the automation to make postmortem cost attribution easier.

emma: Another runbook addition: when queue backlog + pod churn coincide, run quick check on batch-job schedule: `kubectl get cronjob -n batch -o wide` and pause suspicious jobs: `kubectl patch cronjob <name> -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`.

kai: For reliability: implement a circuit-breaker in routing layer that stops ramping beyond 30% if error-rate > 1% for 2m. Also add a synthetic healthcheck for KV cache latency as an early signal.

alex: For follow-ups, owners and deadlines: 
- kai: quota + circuit-breaker impl — due 2026-04-02
- emma: backlog alert + synthetic KV check — due 2026-03-30
- alex: runbook + cost tag automation + pre-warm docs — due 2026-03-29
- lee: create a nightly DR dry-run calendar entry to test traffic shifts (first run next week) — due 2026-03-25

lee: Quick status: traffic shift to AMS at 10%/min started. p95 in SFO dropping, AMS tail stable so far.

emma: Marking follow-up tasks in the incident board. I'll start the post-incident doc after the system stabilizes. :memo:

alex: Thanks all. After stabilization let's add a short playbook section titled 'capacity-drain — immediate steps' listing: cordon+drain nodes, pause batch cronjobs, shift traffic ramp, attach cost tags, escalate to infra if kernel OOM observed.

devops: Will add automation to attach `failover_reason` tags in the next deployment. Also recommend a retrospective on batch job scheduling and preemption policies to avoid future capacity storms.

sre_oncall_bot: Incident INC-2026-17760 transitioned to MONITORING. Next: postmortem to be filed in #postmortems within 72h.

alex: Closing this thread for action tracking — opening a separate postmortem thread with raw metrics + cost breakdown. :lock:
